<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par115 />''tabernacle was reared up''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהָמִית אֶת־דָּוִד|translate=that they should slay David}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=38|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=15|verse=4|hidebook=1}}; with a negative, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=לְבִלְתִּי עֲשׂוֹת אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֹתַי|translate=so that ye will not do all my commandments}}; with the accusative of the personal pronoun, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=29|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=לְמַ֫עַן הָקִיס־אֹֽתְךָ|translate=that he may establish thee}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=24|verse=7}}; with a verbal suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהָרְגֵ֫נִי|translate=to kill me}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=לְבִלְתִּי הֲשִׁיבֵ֫נִי|translate=that he would not cause me to return}} (on the suffix, cf. c). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=6}} the object even precedes the infinitive with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}; on this order cf. the note on {{GHGpar|114|r}}.—If the verb governs a double accusative, the infinitive may also take the same, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=39}} {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרֵי הוֹדִ֫יעַ אֱלֹהִים֖ אֽוֹתְךָ אֶת־כָּל־זֹאת|translate=forasmuch as God hath showed thee all this}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=16}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|115|b}}
Rem. 1. The object after the infinitive construct must also always be regarded as in the accusative, even when it is not expressly introduced (as inall the above examples) by the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־}}, and when therefore the substantive in question might easily be taken as the ''genitive of the object'' governed by the infinitive (the usual construction in Arabic), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=21|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=עֲשׂוֹת מִשְׁפָּט|translate=to do judgement}}. Against regarding it as a genitive, which is in itself possible (''the doing, the executing of judgement''), is the fact (''a'') that elsewhere the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}} is so frequently added; (''b'') that in such a case the secondary forms of the infinitive, such as {{GHGheb|text=רְאֹה}} for ({{GHGheb|text=פָּנֶ֫יךָ}}) {{GHGheb|text=רְאֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=11}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=101|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=16|verse=16}}), would be unintelligible; (''c'') that certain infinitive forms, if they were to be regarded as in the construct state, could hardly retain the pretonic Qameṣ without exception, whereas, when connected with suffixes (i.e. with real genitives; cf. {{GHGpar|33|c}}), this Qameṣ necessarily becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהָמִית צַדִּיק|translate=to slay the righteous}} (never as {{GHGheb|text=לַֽהֲמִית}}; cf., on the other hand, above, {{GHGheb|text=הֲשִׁיבֵ֫נִי}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=21|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=44|verse=30}}. Similarly in such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=13}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=50|verse=4}}) instead of {{GHGheb|text=לָדִין עַמִּים}} we should rather expect {{GHGheb|text=לְדִין}}, if the infinitive were regarded as in the construct state, and {{GHGheb|text=עַמִּים}} as the genitive. Hence also in cases like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=58|verse=9}} ({{GHGheb|text=שְׁלַח}} for {{GHGheb|text=שְׁלֹחַ}}) we must assume, with Sellin, op. cit., p. 78, a merely ‘external phonetic connexion’ and not the genitive construction.

{{GHGmargin-letter|115|c}}
2. The verbal suffixes added to the infinitive are (with the exception of {{GHGheb|text=לְהֽוֹצִאֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=39|verse=14}}) only the suffix of the 1st pers. sing. (besides the above examples cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=27|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=12|verse=17}}, &c.) and plural; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְהַשְׁמִידֵ֫נוּ|translate=to destroy us}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=27}} (immediately after {{GHGheb|text=לָתֵת אֹתָ֫נוּ}}, so that {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ נוּ}} is doubtless a {{GHGterm|verbal}} not a ''noun''-suffix, although in form it might be either); {{GHGheb|text=לַֽהֲמִיתֵ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=23}} (after {{GHGheb|text=חָפֵץ}}). Elsewhere the pronominal object is appended either by means of the accusative sign (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּלֶ֫דֶת אֹתָם}} prop. ''in the bearing them''; {{GHGheb|text=לָדַ֫עַת אֹתִי|translate=to know me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=24|verse=7}}) or in the form of a noun-suffix (as genitive of the object). The latter occurs almost always, whenever the context excludes the possibility of a misunderstanding; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=33}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהַכֹּתוֹ}} (prop. for his smiting) ''to smite him'', not, as the form might also mean, ''in order that he might smite''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=35}}; with the suffix of the 3rd sing. fem. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=25}}; of the 3rd plur. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=2}}, &c. Hence also the suffixes of the 2nd sing. with the infinitive, as {{GHGheb|text=לְהַכֹּֽתְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=14}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=13}}, and even {{GHGheb|text=גַּדֶּלְךָ|translate=to magnify thee}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=7}}, must certainly be regarded as ''nominal'' not {{GHGterm|verbal}} suffixes. The connexion of the noun-suffix, as genitive of the object, with the infinitive,<section end=par115 /><noinclude>
